solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hoodwinks detective with naughty piece of intrigue

parts.note: to con someone is to hoodwink them, so hoodwinks gives cons
PI is a private investigator, a detective
racy means risqué or naughty

explanation.surface: A tale of a fraudster and a sleuth caught up in some saucy scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot hatched in secret by several people is a classic piece of intrigue.

clue.text: One maybe fired youngster on track?

definitions.meaning: a make of revolver, something that is fired
a young male horse, which may race on a track

explanation.surface: Something shot off, perhaps a junior runner at the athletics track.
explanation.definitionFit: The revolver brand and the young racehorse share one name, so each half points to it.

clue.text: No increase before first of December is made official

parts.note: no increase is 'not a rise', run together

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of December is taken

explanation.surface: A pay freeze announced ahead of December becomes formal policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A document certified by a notary has been officially attested, made official.

clue.text: Switching iPods, entertain the idea each person has a lot

definitions.text: the idea each person has a lot

indicators.note: switching tells us the letters of the two words are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swapping music players while musing that everyone owns plenty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is not 'plenty' but one's lot, one's fate: the belief that everyone's fate is fixed in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine that each person's fate is fixed beforehand is the notion that everyone has an allotted lot.

clue.text: Fiddle around in piece of Gothic fiction

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval fiddle-like instrument
ca, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: Someone fiddling about inside a spooky novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne du Maurier's novel of a haunting first wife at Manderley is a Gothic classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Du Maurier's 1938 novel, set in a brooding mansion, is a celebrated Gothic tale.

clue.text: Passengers look over area in part of deck

indicators.note: in tells us the pair goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a card is one part of a deck of cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, look placed over area puts its letters above, so first

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Travellers inspect a space on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship, but it is a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The full complement of people riding in a vehicle is its load of passengers.

clue.text: Care and affection boxing a cosmetic product

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letters go round the a

parts.note: TLC, tender loving care, is care and affection

explanation.surface: A tender pampering session involving a beauty product.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered talc is sold as a cosmetic for the skin, a toiletry item.

clue.text: Drive past houses in great quantities

indicators.note: houses means contains, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ago means in the past
to go is to drive or travel

explanation.surface: A motorist cruises by a row of homes on a grand scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in abundance, as in drinks flowing freely and plentifully.

clue.text: The fickle English, digging into fruit after tea

indicators.note: after places the fruit piece following the tea piece

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: digging into means pushing inside the fruit

parts.note: melons are fruit

explanation.surface: Changeable English folk tucking into fruit after their cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Lizards that change colour lend their name to people who keep shifting views, the changeable.

clue.text: As insolent as it could be eye-catching

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be made into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Being as rude as possible draws attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid, attention-grabbing reporting is sensational, designed to catch the eye.

clue.text: Most of second drink

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the latter is the second of two

explanation.surface: Nearly all of a follow-up beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso coffee is a common café drink.

clue.text: Side of real bacon chopped up

indicators.note: chopped up suggests cutting into pieces, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A flank of genuine bacon diced for cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a cut of bacon, but it is a football team, the Spanish club.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a famous football club, a team or side.

clue.text: Penned by novelist, put out fake safety guide

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the letters sit inside the novelist

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist
put out means annoyed, cross
cod as an adjective means fake or mock

explanation.surface: A writer annoyed at a bogus set of rules for keeping safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Green Cross Code is the UK road-safety drill taught to children for crossing roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's road-crossing rules for children are a set of safety instructions.

clue.text: Defence playing worst during counterattack

indicators.note: during places the scrambled letters within the counterattack word

parts.note: a break in sport is a rapid counterattack

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are not in their proper order and are mixed

explanation.surface: A football side defending badly while hit on the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' sounds like the football side's back line, but it is a field fortification; a break is a fast counterattack in football.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastwork is a low temporary fortification, a defensive wall.

clue.text: Rashid once put in list

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
to set is to put

explanation.surface: Someone named Rashid was once placed on a roster.
explanation.walkthrough: Rashid is the Egyptian town once called Rosetta, where the Rosetta Stone was found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian port now called Rashid was formerly known by this European name.

clue.text: Bill in valley is worth seeing?

indicators.note: in puts the bill inside the valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley
a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: An invoice from the dales is worth a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is meant as dating someone, as in 'are you seeing anyone?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attractive enough to go out with is worth seeing romantically.

clue.text: In poker, stakes pool of money in area of ignorance

parts.note: blinds are compulsory stakes put up before the deal in poker
the pot is the pool of money bet in a game

explanation.surface: A poker table where the stakes form a pool of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject one knows nothing about is a gap or weak spot in knowledge.

clue.text: Ready to consume drink, eating dip

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the drink surrounds the dip

parts.note: ale is a drink
a dent is a dip or hollow

explanation.surface: A beer that has been taking in a snack dip is ready to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta cooked firm to the bite is done and ready for eating.

clue.text: Keep up home, retaining old hedging

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to save is to keep

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Maintaining an old house while keeping options open.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedging is avoiding a straight answer, ducking the question.

clue.text: African men from Wales and Scotland?

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether some Welsh and Scots chaps came from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivory Coast in West Africa.

clue.text: Understanding son during brief stay at hotel?

indicators.note: during puts the son within the overnight stay

parts.note: a short hotel stay is one night, with I for one

explanation.surface: A young man gains understanding on a quick overnight visit to a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep grasp or perception, a form of understanding.

clue.text: Book one's vehicles, close by after turning right

indicators.note: after puts the rest of the pieces following the flipped abbreviation
turning means the abbreviation is flipped round

parts.note: one's is I'S, so I and S
trams are vehicles
handy means close by, conveniently near

explanation.surface: Reserving one's cars close by after a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne's comic novel 'The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterne's eighteenth-century novel is a famous book.

clue.text: Keen on securing right start

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Eager to get things off to a correct beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction is the opening section, the beginning of a piece.

clue.text: Busy learner entering school, perhaps

definitions.note: busy is British slang for a police officer, one of the police

indicators.note: entering means going inside

parts.note: a school of whales is a pod, a group of sea creatures
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: An industrious student starting at a new school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is not 'occupied': in UK slang a busy is a police officer, and plod is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a policeman, as is the other slang word, both from crime fiction.

clue.text: Proving smarter than vamp exposing clothes

indicators.note: clothes means dresses or covers, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: outing someone is exposing them
a fox is an attractive woman, a vamp

explanation.surface: Getting the better of a seductress by revealing what she wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is a verb: OUTING clothes FOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwitting someone with cunning is getting the better of them, being cleverer.

clue.text: Terror the French revolutionary is to drive forward

parts.note: a terror is a mischievous child, an imp

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French Revolution's Terror pushed events onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terror' and 'revolutionary' call up the French Revolution, but the terror is a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge onwards, propel.

clue.text: Recognise obsessive specialist from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read right to left

parts.note: a wonk is an obsessive expert, as in a policy wonk

explanation.surface: Spotting a nerdy expert arriving from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise someone is to be acquainted with them, be familiar.

clue.text: Started diet — it gets broken with nuts

indicators.note: gets broken suggests smashing apart the letters and putting them in a new order

explanation.surface: A diet abandoned because of a nut binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'gets broken' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute something is to set it up or begin it, so started fits.
